gen_risks.description: Climate‑induced droughts and floods may force extensions of school summer breaks, reducing instructional days.
gen_risks.mitigation: Build flexible academic calendars, incorporate remote learning options, and develop climate‑resilient school schedules.
gen_risks.evidence: State vulnerable to droughts and floods can force extensions of the annual school summer break (Section B.3).

gen_risks.description: Insufficient in‑service teacher training and shortage of subject‑specialist teachers could limit learning gains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Scale up recruitment, deliver need‑based TaRL and subject‑specific training, and monitor teacher performance through classroom observations.
gen_risks.evidence: Majority of teachers lack adequate in‑service training; many teach multiple grades and subjects (Section B.11).

gen_risks.description: Low enrollment of boys in senior secondary science and commerce streams may increase dropout rates.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish model composite schools with residential facilities for boys and provide scholarships to improve access.
gen_risks.evidence: High dropout rates among boys due to limited access to quality science and commerce education (Section B.6).

gen_risks.description: Complex multi‑agency fiduciary and procurement arrangements may cause fund‑release delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen FM staffing, enforce internal audit, and adopt clear procurement plans with timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Multiple tiers of planning and limited capacities result in inadequately planned budgeting and fund‑release delays (Section 59).

gen_risks.description: Absence of annual procurement plans could lead to untimely contract awards and cost overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate preparation and public disclosure of annual procurement plans per the FMP Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: No practice of preparing an annual procurement plan was observed (Section 4.4).

gen_risks.description: Civil works may generate waste, fire‑safety gaps, and non‑compliant construction affecting environmental and social outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply green building guidelines, conduct EHS training, and monitor waste management during construction.
gen_risks.evidence: Gaps in fire safety, waste management, and lack of disaster‑resilient design identified (Sections 67‑68).

gen_risks.description: Inadequate protection of personal data collected through EMIS and assessments could breach privacy regulations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct data‑protection impact analysis, implement encryption, access controls, and align with national data‑privacy laws.
gen_risks.evidence: Operations involving personal data must be carried out with due regard to legal framework (Legal Covenants, Section V).

gen_risks.description: Weak verification capacity may delay DLI achievement verification and subsequent disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure timely appointment of Independent Verification Agency, provide training on verification protocols, and set clear reporting timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: IVAs will verify DLI results; verification protocols outlined (Section 45‑46).

gen_risks.description: Insufficient community engagement and grievance redress could lead to stakeholder dissatisfaction and project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen GRM, implement community‑led social audit tool, and hold regular stakeholder consultations.
gen_risks.evidence: Need for strengthening grievance redress mechanism and community‑led social audits (Sections 70‑75).

gen_risks.description: Reliance on under‑funded technical support agencies may limit capacity‑building effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Negotiate clear contracts with performance milestones, secure adequate funding, and plan for knowledge transfer to nodal institutions.
gen_risks.evidence: Technical support agencies are under‑funded, lack scalability, and have limited contracts (Section 4.4, point 4).

gen_risks.description: High proportion of budget allocated to salaries limits resources for quality improvements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Leverage PforR incentives to re‑allocate savings from economies of scale and prioritize quality‑related expenditures.
gen_risks.evidence: 84.8% of consolidated budget used for salaries, limiting funds for quality improvements (Section A.18).

gen_risks.description: Potential policy shifts or political changes could affect alignment with NEP 2020 and funding commitments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous dialogue with central and state education ministries and embed NEP objectives in statutory agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Operation aligns with NEP 2020 and CPF; political alignment noted (Section 15).

gen_risks.description: Construction timelines may be disrupted by extreme weather events, delaying school upgrades.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include weather‑contingency buffers in schedules and adopt disaster‑resilient design standards.
gen_risks.evidence: State vulnerable to climate events; civil works designed with disaster‑resilient features (Sections B.3, 34).

gen_risks.description: Teacher training outcomes may not translate into improved classroom practice without robust monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement TEACH classroom observation tool, periodic sample observations, and feedback loops for continuous improvement.
gen_risks.evidence: Monitoring of TaRL training will use TEACH tool and classroom observations (Section 52).

gen_risks.description: Corruption or fraud risks in procurement due to limited transparency and weak complaint handling.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank anti‑corruption guidelines, publish contract awards, and establish an online procurement complaint portal.
gen_risks.evidence: Anti‑corruption guidelines apply; procurement complaint handling currently weak (Sections 64‑65).

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk is rated Substantial. State elections are due in December 2023 and the associated large democratic exercise could slow down activities envisioned for the first year of the operation. The window between the operation being declared effective and the state elections is small.
gt_risks.mitigation: Disruptions are expected to be minimal given that the state intends to initiate work and complete necessary field work and/or data collection well before the elections, and utilize the election period for analysis and training module/materials development. The implementing bodies (SIS-SS, SCERT, SIEMAT, and SAC) will need to move swiftly to realize the state's plans.

gt_risks.description: Technical Design of operation risk is rated Substantial. Certain context-specific attributes such as topography and underlying community representation in overall enrolment could raise challenges, including barriers to school enrolment such as lack of physical access in sparsely populated areas with poor road connectivity, or high opportunity cost of schooling due to informal-sector employment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Government of Chhattisgarh has addressed similar challenges in the past through development and rollout of customized solutions; the project will enable planning for residential facilities for students and teachers in model schools in topographically hard-to-reach areas.

gt_risks.description: Institutional Capacity for Implementation and Sustainability risk is rated Substantial. In some cases, nodal educational institutions lack the expertise to implement technically complex interventions.
gt_risks.mitigation: Onboarding a Program Management Consultant (PMC) and technical support agencies is expected to significantly reduce the risks involved. Sustainability post-completion will be ensured through careful planning, technical support for capacity building of nodal institutions, and institutionalizing new mechanisms.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. Considering the implementing arrangements and diverse capacity across implementing agencies, implementation constraints can be foreseen in public financial management arrangements and compliance with rules and regulations for accountability.
gt_risks.mitigation: Focused attention in the short/medium term on enhanced effectiveness of planning, budgeting, and fund flow processes; adequacy of staffing and capacity building of fiduciary staff; strengthened monitoring through internal and external independent reviews; timely resolution of independent external review observations; a robust dedicated procurement complaints redressal system; strengthened contract management for delivery of goods and works; and ensuring exclusion of Bank-debarred firms from high-value contracts.
